reasons: Both answers identify the Montana WDEA good-cause problem, explain why Montana law governs, and give concrete pre-Friday steps with a release, policy check and counsel review, so they meet every rubric item. B dates the key WDEA amendments correctly (2021), where A twice says 2019. B also adds useful practical warnings: no backdated write-ups, OWBPA timing means he won't sign on Friday, and a check for EPLI notice requirements. A frames the grievance-procedure mechanism a little more accurately, but that doesn't outweigh its dating error.

B: Describes providing the internal grievance procedure within 7 days as a WDEA requirement, when it is a condition for requiring the employee to exhaust internal remedies
Implies 'failure to perform job duties satisfactorily' was added to good cause in 2021; it was already part of the original definition
